sentences.text:
Author: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
Bench: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 And
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Laxmi Narayana Alishetty
 L.A.A.S.No.108 Of 2007
Judgment:

(Per Hon'ble Sri Justice Laxmi Narayana Alishetty) This appeal, under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short, 'the Act'), is filed by the Government through the Land Acquisition Officer (HUDA), Hyderabad, aggrieved by the order and decree, dated 10.11.2005, passed in O.P.No.2 of 1993 by the learned Senior Civil Judge, Sangareddy (for short, 'the reference Court').
2. Heard Ms. D. Madhavi, learned Standing Counsel for HMDA, appearing for the appellant.
3.

The brief facts of the case are that the Hyderabad Urban Development Authority had sent a requisition to the Collector, Medak District, for acquisition of Ac.528-24 guntas of agricultural land situated at Tellapur Village, Ramachandrapuram Mandal, Medak District, including the land admeasuring Ac.1-12 guntas in Survey No.344 (for short, 'the subject land') belonging to the respondents- claimants, for the purpose of expansion of Ramachandrapuram Ring Town Residential Complex, Phase-V.
Accordingly, the Land Acquisition Officer has initiated proceedings under the Act and 2 AKS,J & LNA,J notification under Section 4(1) of the Act was issued on 11.07.1984.
The Land Acquisition Officer, after conducting necessary enquiry, passed Award No.4 of 1989, dated 04.08.1989, fixing the market value for the subject land at Rs.20,000/- per acre.
The possession of the subject land was taken on 20.12.1989.

4. Not satisfied with the compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Officer, the respondents-claimants sought reference under Section 18 of the Act and the same was numbered as O.P.No.2 of 1993 on the file of the reference Court.
5. Before the reference Court, on behalf of the respondents- claimants, PWs.1 and 2 were examined and Exs.A1 to A5 were marked.
On behalf of the Land Acquisition Officer, RW.1 was examined and Ex.B1 was marked.

6. The reference Court, considering the oral and documentary evidence on record, vide impugned order and decree, dated 10.11.2005, enhanced the market value fixed by the Land Acquisition Officer from Rs.20,000/- per acre to Rs.18/- per Square Yard with a deduction of Rs.6/- per Square Yard towards developmental charges, apart from granting all statutory benefits as per the Act.
Aggrieved by the same, the present appeal is filed by the Government through the Land Acquisition Thegovt.

Learned Standing Counsel appearing for the appellant had contended that aggrieved by the compensation granted by the Land Acquisition Officer by the very same Award, dated 04.08.1989,
the owners in respect of other lands sought reference under Section 18 of the Act and the reference Court instead of clubbing all the O.Ps. had decided the said O.Ps. on different dates, which is not permissible under law.

Learned Standing Counsel had further contended that the District Judge,
Medak at Sangareddy, vide order, dated 16.04.1999, passed in O.P.No.38 of 1993 has enhanced the compensation in respect of some of the acquired lands from Rs.20,000/- per acre to Rs.26,000/-
per acre, whereas in the present case, the reference Court had erroneously enhanced the compensation to Rs.12/- per Square Yard.

The reference Court ought to have fixed the market value for the subject land at Rs.26,000/- per acre in terms of the order, dated 16.04.1999, passed in O.P.No.38 of 1993 and ultimately, prayed to allow the appeal.

8. A perusal of the material placed on record discloses that the Land Acquisition Officer by relying on the Sale Deed bearing Document No.1998/84, dated 26.04.1984, by which land admeasuring Ac.1-20 guntas in Survey No.368/EE situated at 4 AKS,J & LNA,J Tellapur Village was sold for Rs.30,000/- i.e. Rs.20,000/- per acre, fixed the market value for the entire acquired lands at Rs.20,000/- per acre.

Aggrieved by the same, some of the claimants filed O.P.No.314 of 1993 and batch before the Principal District Judge, Medak at Sangareddy, and the learned Principal District Judge vide order, dated 29.03.2004, had enhanced the market value to Rs.12/- per Square Yard.

entities.text: Principal District Judge, Medak at Sangareddy
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The respondents-claimants in their evidence have categorically stated that the subject land is similar in nature and has same potentiality to that of the lands covered under O.P.No.314 of 1993 and batch.

The reference Court, considering the oral and documentary evidence on record and considering the fact that the subject land is similar in nature and potentiality to that of the lands covered under O.P.No.314 of 1993 and batch and that they form part of the same notification and Award, fixed the market value for the subject land at Rs.12/- per Square Yard, by relying on the order, dated 29.03.2004, passed in O.P.No.314 of 1993 and batch.
Therefore, the reference Court has rightly fixed the compensation at Rs.12/- per Square Yard for the subject land and the respondents- claimants cannot be discriminated in awarding compensation.

9. Further, the contention raised by the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the appellant that the reference Court ought to have passed common judgment in all the O.Ps. filed against the very 5 AKS,J & LNA,J same Award, dated 04.08.1989, is not tenable.
The subject land as well as the lands covered under O.P.No.314 of 1993 and batch are similar in nature and potentiality and are acquired by the same notification.

10. Here, it is relevant to refer to the decision of the Honourable Supreme Court in Ali Mohammad Beigh and others v. State of Jammu and Kashmir 1, wherein the Honourable Supreme Court had observed that when the lands are more or less situated nearby and when the acquired lands are identical and similar and the acquisition is for the same purpose, it would not be proper to discriminate between the landowners, unless there are strong reasons.

entities.text: Ali Mohammad Beigh and others v. State of Jammu and Kashmir 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Honourable Supreme Thegovt.
Of A.P., vs Pandu Goud on 9 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88131736/

2 Court had also observed that when the lands are acquired at the same time and for the same purpose and though the lands are situated in different Villages, if the lands are similar, it would be unfair to discriminate between the landowners.
11. In the present case, the subject land and the lands covered under O.P.No.314 of 1993 and batch were acquired under the same notification and for the same purpose and a common Award was passed.
It is also evident from the record that both the lands form part of Tellapur Village and are similar in nature and potentiality.
(2017) 4 SCC 717 6 AKS,J & LNA,J
Therefore, the respondents-claimants are entitled to the very same compensation as awarded in O.P.No.314 of 1993 and batch, dated 29.03.2004.
Therefore, in considered opinion of this Court, there are no merits in the appeal and the same is liable to be dismissed.
12. Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous Applications, if any, pending in this appeal shall stand closed.
